en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Itthivimāna Section.
6. Vihāravimānavatthu “With a most excellent complexion... [as before] ...”
Like stars and medicinal herbs,
from every limb of hers as she danced, [light radiated forth].
Divine sounds, worthy of being heard and delightful, issue forth as she dances.
From every limb,
divine fragrances waft forth—
pure scents, delightful to the mind.
As they are being twisted off from the body,
the sound of those ornaments upon their braided hair is heard.
Just as when a fivefold musical ensemble is played,
the ornaments, shaken by the wind,
are made to tremble by the wind.
The sound of them is heard like that of a fivefold musical ensemble;
even the garland upon their heads—
Purely fragrant and delightful,
its scent wafts in all directions,
like that of the mañjūsaka tree.
From the scent you perceive that pure fragrance and see that superhuman form;
O deity, being questioned, please explain.
“Venerable sir, what is the fruit of this deed? “In Sāvatthī, venerable sir,
I had a friend who built a great monastery for the Saṅgha.”
Having seen that, and having faith therein, I rejoiced, even though this home was dear to me.
By that very pure rejoicing of mine, [I attained this fruit].
Having obtained this wondrous palace, beautiful to behold,
it travels sixteen yojanas in every direction through the air by means of my psychic power.
My dwellings are gabled houses,
divided into sections and measured out;
they shine forth, resplendent.
For a hundred yojanas all around,
there is a lotus pond here frequented by large fish.
With clear water, perfectly serene,
strewn with golden sand,
and covered with various lotuses.
Covered with white lotuses,
they waft fragrant scents,
delightful when stirred by the breeze.
Jambu trees, panasa trees, tāla trees,
and groves of coconut palms grew within the inner courtyard.
Various trees were planted there,
resounding with the music of diverse instruments and filled with the voices of throngs of celestial nymphs.
Even the man who might see me in a dream would be filled with joy.
Such a sight is truly wonderful to behold.
This celestial mansion, radiant in every way,
has been produced by my own deeds;
it is sufficient, therefore, to perform meritorious acts.
“By that very pure rejoicing of yours,
you have obtained this marvelous and wonderful celestial mansion;
indeed, it is because of her who gave that gift, the woman— ”
“Tell me her destiny: where has she been reborn?
“O Venerable One, she who was my friend built a great monastery for the Saṅgha.”
Having understood the Dhamma, she gave a gift;
she was reborn among the Nimmānarati devas.
She was the wife of that Sunimmita.
The ripening of kamma for her is inconceivable;
as to where Sāti has been reborn, which you ask me—
this I have explained to you exactly as it is, not otherwise.
Therefore, you too should encourage others:
give gifts to the Sangha with your wealth,
and listen to the Dhamma with a serene mind.
The attainment of human birth is very difficult to obtain, yet it has been gained.
He who taught the path that masters the path—
possessing the voice of Brahmā and skin like refined gold— has appeared.
Give gifts to the Saṅgha with wealth;
there, offerings become of great fruit.
Those eight persons who are praised by the virtuous—
These four constitute the pairs;
they are the disciples of the Sugata worthy of offerings.
What is given to them yields great fruit.
The four who have entered the path and the four who stand in the fruit—
this is the Saṅgha, upright.
Established in wisdom and virtue,
[he is the refuge] for people who perform sacrifices and for living beings seeking merit.
Merit based on the acquisitions that one has performed,
when given to the Saṅgha, is of great fruit;
for this Saṅgha is vast and sublime.
He is immeasurable like the ocean, the great sea;
these disciples, the heroes among men,
are supreme because they proclaim the Dhamma that brings light.
Well given, well offered, well sacrificed is that gift which they give dedicated to the Saṅgha;
that offering, directed toward the Saṅgha, is firmly established.
Of great fruit, they are praised by those who know the world.
Remembering such a sacrifice as this,
those born of the Vedas wander throughout the world.
"Having removed the stain of stinginess along with its root,
the blameless ones go to the heavenly state.
The sixth Vimāna, the Mansion of the Monastery.
The second recitation section.
